paper_title: dKV-Cache The Cache for Diffusion Language Models
caption: (left) and (right) on GSM8K with different settings: decoding length L, sampling steps S, refresh intervals and the window size.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the trade-off between performance (measured as accuracy in percentage) and speed (measured in tokens per second) for different configurations of the dKV-Cache system on the GSM8K benchmark. The x-axis, labeled "Speed (Tokens/s)", is linearly scaled from approximately 20 to 160 tokens per second, with tick marks every 20 units. The y-axis, labeled "Performance (Accuracy %)", is also linearly scaled from 65% to 85%, with tick marks every 5 percentage points. Five distinct line styles represent different cache refresh intervals: "w/o Cache" (blue crosses), "Refresh=2" (blue squares), "Refresh=4" (light blue circles), "Refresh=8" (purple diamonds), and "Refresh=16" (gray stars). These configurations show varying levels of accuracy and speed, with the "w/o Cache" line achieving the highest accuracy (around 83%) at low speed (~20 tokens/s), and the "Refresh=16" line exhibiting lower accuracy (~67%) at higher speed (~160 tokens/s). Additionally, five colored lines with different markers represent configurations with specific decoding lengths L and sampling steps S: L=512, S=512 (blue solid), L=512, S=256 (dashed blue), L=512, S=128 (dotted blue), L=128, S=64 (red solid), and L=128, S=32 (dashed red). These lines show a general downward trend in accuracy as speed increases. Two Pareto front curves are also shown: the "LLaDA Pareto Front" (dotted black) and the "Cache Pareto Front" (dashed black), which outline the optimal trade-offs between performance and speed for their respective systems. The "Cache Pareto Front" starts at approximately 83% accuracy at 20 tokens/s and decreases to 65% accuracy at 160 tokens/s, while the "LLaDA Pareto Front" starts at about 82% accuracy at 20 tokens/s and drops sharply to around 65% at 90 tokens/s, after which it is not shown.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the trade-off between performance (accuracy, in percentage) and speed (tokens per second) for different configurations of the dKV-Cache system on the GSM8K benchmark, under varying decoding length (L), sampling steps (S), and refresh intervals. The x-axis represents Speed (Tokens/s), ranging from 0 to 160 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 20. The y-axis represents Performance (Accuracy %), ranging from 60 to 85 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 5. Five colored lines with distinct markers represent different (L, S) pairs: blue circles for L=512, S=512; light blue squares for L=512, S=256; red squares for L=128, S=64; pink circles for L=128, S=32. Additionally, two dashed lines represent baseline or reference curves: a dotted black line labeled "LLaDA Pareto Front" and a dash-dotted black line labeled "Cache Pareto Front". The legend also includes a separate legend for refresh intervals: gray markers with crosses for "w/o Cache", gray squares for "Refresh=2", gray circles for "Refresh=4", gray diamonds for "Refresh=8", and gray triangles for "Refresh=16", though these are not directly plotted as separate lines but may correspond to the data points on the curves. The blue line (L=512, S=512) starts at approximately 80% accuracy at 20 tokens/s and declines to about 75% at 60 tokens/s, then drops more steeply to around 70% at 100 tokens/s. The light blue line (L=512, S=256) begins at 80% accuracy at 20 tokens/s and decreases to about 75% at 40 tokens/s, then continues to decline to 70% at 80 tokens/s. The red line (L=128, S=64) starts at 75% accuracy at 40 tokens/s and remains relatively flat, ending at 70% accuracy at 120 tokens/s. The pink line (L=128, S=32) begins at 70% accuracy at 60 tokens/s and remains nearly constant, ending at 65% accuracy at 160 tokens/s. The "LLaDA Pareto Front" (dotted black line) starts at approximately 80% accuracy at 20 tokens/s and decreases linearly to 65% at 160 tokens/s. The "Cache Pareto Front" (dash-dotted black line) follows a similar trend, starting at 80% accuracy at 20 tokens/s and decreasing to 65% at 160 tokens/s, closely tracking the LLaDA front.
